title: Boldness
speaker: Pastor Tito Lyro

outline.title: The Context of the Vav Section
subpoints: Hebrew poetic structure uses the conjunction 'and' (Vav) in every verse
Grammatical structure differs from previous sections with two verses per sentence
Content remains substantive despite structural repetition

outline.title: Prayer for Boldness: Faithfulness Anchored in Mercy
subpoints: Boldness is rooted in God's covenantal faithfulness (Hesed)
God's mercy is based on His name and promises, not human merit
The prayer seeks salvation and strength according to God's word

outline.title: Answering Reproaches with God's Word
subpoints: Believers must trust in Scripture to answer critics and mockers
The fear of man should be replaced by the fear of God's disapproval
Every believer is called to articulate the gospel clearly (1 Peter 3:15)

outline.title: Commitment to Boldness in Opposition
subpoints: The psalmist commits to keeping God's law continually
Obedience is an eternal activity and training for heaven
Boldness involves speaking truth even when it leads to persecution

summary:
In this sermon, Pastor Tito Lyro explores the Vav section of Psalm 119 (verses 41-48), focusing on the theme of boldness in the face of opposition. He notes that while the Hebrew structure of this section is repetitive due to the use of the conjunction 'and,' the content is profound, presenting a prayer for the grace to stand firm in faith. The message emphasizes that true boldness is not self-generated but is anchored in God's covenantal faithfulness (Hesed) and His steadfast love, which remains constant regardless of human inconsistency.

The sermon distinguishes between a prayer for boldness and a commitment to boldness. The psalmist prays for the ability to answer reproaches and to keep the word of truth in his mouth, recognizing that a believer's defense of the faith must be rooted in Scripture rather than personal eloquence. This aligns with the New Testament command in 1 Peter 3:15 to be ready to give a reason for the hope that lies within, a responsibility that applies to every believer who knows the objective facts of the gospel.

Finally, the message addresses the reality of persecution in a broken world. Rather than praying for a trouble-free life, the faithful are called to pray for the grace to speak and live God's truth amidst difficulties. The psalmist’s commitment to keep God's law 'forever and ever' serves as a model for the Christian life, where obedience is viewed as an eternal activity and a preparation for heaven, requiring believers to walk in liberty and boldness even when facing societal opposition.
